project.name: Stamford Historic Town Explorer

properties.name: Stamford curated visitor boundary
properties.methodology: Morphological closing of the preserved official built-up-area geometry using a 300 metre outward and inward buffer. This fills internal omissions for connected parks, river corridors and visitor green spaces without applying a general outward town buffer.

project.boundarySource: Curated Stamford visitor boundary derived from ONS Built-up Areas (December 2024)
project.researchNotes: Townscape Guides audit completed 2026-08-09. The unchanged ONS 2024 built-up area is the active inclusion boundary. Historic England designations and public current OpenStreetMap visitor facilities were filtered point-in-polygon.

touristAppeal.label: Destination draw
touristAppeal.summary: One of England’s strongest small historic towns: an unusually complete stone-built centre, landmark churches, independent shops, riverside meadows and a first-rate self-guided trail justify a journey in their own right.

townGuide.headline: Honey-stone streets, church towers and riverside meadows
townGuide.intro: Stamford rewards an unhurried day on foot. Move between Georgian and medieval streets, market squares and landmark churches, then drop to the Welland and the Meadows for a greener view of the town.
perfectFor: A genuine destination town, especially for visitors who enjoy architecture, markets and compact walks.

suggestedFirstVisit.title: Market squares, All Saints and the Meadows
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Begin around Red Lion Square and All Saints, thread south through the stone streets and St Martin’s, then return beside the Welland and Stamford Meadows.

dontMiss: Stamford historic townscape and market squares

This is a visitor extent, not an administrative replacement.
